_README: ⛔ GAP-8 — the scan floors. Each entry is the non-blank line count the gate READ after stripping. A gate reading less than its floor has gone blind and reds; see scripts/lib/scanFloor.ts. ⚠ WHY A 5% MARGIN AND NOT THE EXACT MEASUREMENT: these counts are 1k–70k lines and move with every ordinary commit, so an exact floor would red permanently and train people to raise the number without reading it — the failure web-e2e.yml's header records killing the previous lane. The margin still catches the failure being guarded: total blinding drops the count to ~0, and losing a root or an extension drops it by far more than 5%. ⛔ The floor is DOWNWARD-ONLY: lowering it needs a stated reason, exactly like HOSTILE_FLOOR.

conflict-markers.why: S1.12.11. ⛔ This gate does NOT strip its input — a marker inside a comment is still an unresolved conflict — so lint:scan-floors would not have demanded a floor. It carries one anyway, because the failure it guards is the one it was written for: a scan whose population goes empty reports ZERO markers and exits 0, which reads identically to a clean tree. Population is `git ls-files`, so the blinding mode is `git` returning nothing or the skip-set swallowing an extension; both drop the count far past 5%. Margin per the _README.

restore-doors.why: Measured 2026-08-29 at S1.11.4.3 on the gate's first green run. Floor is 95% of the measured count — see the ledger header for why a margin and not the exact figure. ⛔ Verified the same way as its siblings: blanking lib/stripCode's exports drops the count to ~0 and this gate reds instead of reporting a clean four-door surface it never read.

rounding.why: S1.12.5.6 [pass-5 A5-4]. Wired because lint:scan-floors REFUSED this gate on its first run - it strips its input and had no floor, which is GAP-8: a gate that strips can report a pass while reading nothing. Its own downward-only cap does not protect it, and in fact inverts: a scan that suddenly reads zero files reports FEWER copies, and the gate would then ask someone to lower the cap to match. 5% margin per the _README.

amount-collapse.why: S1.13.7.8 [pass-6 C1-6]. This gate STRIPS comments — load-bearing, because both its own docblock and PaydayCaptureSheet's quote the banned form while recording the defect, and a guard that reds on its own documentation gets deleted rather than obeyed. Stripping is therefore exactly the blinding mode GAP-8 describes: a stripper that returns blanks makes the sweep find zero collapses and exit 0, indistinguishable from a clean tree. Population is `git ls-files` over apps/rn + packages/core + scripts. Margin per the _README.

store-id-writes.why: S1.13.7.11 [pass-6 A3-3]. Wired on the gate's first run, which lint:scan-floors refused for having no floor - GAP-8, a gate that strips can report a pass while reading nothing. It matters more than usual here because the cap is 0: a scan that reads nothing finds no bare id writes and prints the same green line as a clean tree. 5% margin per the _README.

fixture-dates.why: S1.13.7.12.6 [class-1 re-audit]. This gate began stripping comments when R7 showed a comment could supply a literal's aging key, and lint:scan-floors demanded a floor the same run. MEASURED failing open first, not assumed: against a stripper that blanks everything it printed '0 imminent fuses' and exited 0 - a gate reading nothing reporting the tree clean, which is the exact shape A1-4 shipped. MIN_TEST_FILES does not cover this: the population stays full while every literal inside it vanishes. Margin per the _README.
